correctness.rationale: Every predecessor is a closed labeled walk of the explicit four-state de Bruijn graph; the all-one trace is the Perrin sequence. A zero-edge reduction gives 2x2 transfer matrices H_k, satisfying H_{k+3}=H_{k+1}+H_k. The bivariate recurrence for D(a,b)=H_{a+b+1}-H_aH_b and 19 exact finite positive base matrices establish entrywise merging for all positive indices except ordered (1,2). Any cyclic sequence with at least two positive gaps admits a nonexceptional adjacent pair. Iterative merging bounds every output with a zero by h_{m-1}, which is strictly less than P_n for n>=5. Small cases checked. verify_certificate.py checks the complete finite lemma and direct zero-run transfer; verify_direct.py exhausts every input for n=1..18. Finite enumeration is corroboration, not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The novelty is the sharp global maximum and unique maximizing output for every cyclic length at least five. Powley 2009 implies the homogeneous Perrin count but does not supply the comparison with every heterogeneous output. The indexed Rule 110 preimage matrices are also classical and not claimed as new. The finite-base positive-matrix merger with its one exceptional orientation gives the missing sharp comparison. No equivalent or dominating explicit published statement was found in the actual searches; unindexed or obscure historical tables remain a substantive residual risk.
residual_risks: Historical priority of the all-output extremal inequality has not been independently established; archived software, unindexed papers and unpublished observations may contain it.
The earliest verified public source date is from a dated Rule 110 context source, not a publication date for the new theorem.

value.rationale: Worst-case inverse branching of the computationally universal elementary Rule 110 automaton quantifies a natural reconstruction ambiguity on every cyclic ring. Its unique maximizing output and exact Perrin growth for all n>=5 give more than a special homogeneous-output count: no other cyclic output can match it. The structured transfer-merger proof and exceptional pair are reusable mathematical tools. No multistep or full histogram claims are made.
